title: Procurement & Logistics Officer

title: 50 mila lavoratori negli Emirati. Ecco come l’Etiopia riduce la disoccupazione
description: 50 mila lavoratori saranno inviati negli Emirati Arabi Uniti come parte di un programma per modernizzare la forza lavoro. Lo ha annunciato il primo ministro etiope Abiy Ahmed che in questo modo intende ridurre la disoccupazione nel suo paese. Il premier ha chiarito che, oltre a quelli già previsti, sono in corso negoziati per l'invio di 200 mila lavoratori in tre anni. E ci sarebbero alla finestra, come paesi destinatari, anche alcuni Stati europei e il Giappone. L’idea dell’esecutivo è che in tal modo gli etiopi potranno guadagnare salari migliori e saranno in grado di perfezionare le loro capacità, prima di ritornare ricchi di know-how nel proprio paese di origine. Sullo sfondo le relazioni geopolitiche tra i paesi dell’Africa orientale e quelli mediorientali. E, in particolare, tra Etiopia ed Emirati Arabi Uniti, che nel 2018 si sono impegnati a iniettare 2,6 miliardi di euro nelle casse etiopi. Una possibile parziale spiegazione dell’originale modo scelto dal paese africano per ridurre la disoccupazione.

Background The Disarmament, Demobilization, and Reintegration (DDR) program for Ethiopia was initiated as a crucial step towards implementing the peace agreement signed between the Government of Ethiopia and the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) on 2nd November 2022 in South Africa. This agreement ended the long-standing conflict that had arisen between the TPLF and the central government in Ethiopia, resulting in widespread violence and displacement. The objective of the DDR program is to facilitate the disarmament of former combatants from Tigray, Amhara and Afar, their demobilization and eventual reintegration into civilian life. The program is geared towards restoring peace, promoting reconciliation and creating a conducive environment for sustainable development. Eventual areas of coverage will go beyond Northern Ethiopia and cover other regions of Ethiopia. The Government of Ethiopia has mandated and created the “National Rehabilitation Commission (NRC)” which is responsible for design, planning, implementation, and monitoring of the DDR programme in the country. The overall DDR beneficiaries identified are 371,971. The Government has planned implementation of the programme. In Phase 1, a total of 75,000 combatants will be demobilized in 2024 and the balance will be demobilized in 2025. UNDP is supporting the NRC in close coordination with various national and international partners, including the United Nations, non-governmental organizations, and other actors. It is expected that the DDR program will provide an opportunity for the combatants in North Ethiopia to turn their focus towards peaceful and productive activities, thereby contributing to the overall stability and development of the North Ethiopia region. The DDR program has close linkages with the National Dialogue, Transitional Justice, and Peace Support programme. The DDR programme is anchored in the Governance Unit. title: Project Associate (Protection)

Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants. IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. This position will be based in Dewele Organizational Context and Scope E stablished in 1951, IOM is the leading intergovernmental organization in the field of migration and works closely with governmental, intergovernmental, and non-governmental partners. IOM is dedicated to promoting human and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It does so by providing services and advice to governments and migrants. IOM Ethiopia's vision is to place the rights and well-being of migrants at the centre of its interventions, adopting a preventive, protective, and responsive approach. Its protection interventions in Ethiopia follow a six-pillar intervention that includes direct assistance to migrants, displaced persons and affected communities, thematic guidance, capacity development, advocacy, and research. The Protection Unit (PXU) works closely with the government of Ethiopia and various stakeholders in emergency, displacement, and migration settings to reduce protection risks and address the needs of vulnerable individuals and communities. IOM is guided by rights-based approaches across our migration programming, demonstrating commitment to the safeguarding of vulnerable groups. Within PXU, and under the Migrant Protection and Assistance sub-unit, non-emergenciies, programming areas include Counter-trafficking, Assistance to Vulnerable Migrants (AVM), and Community Outreach. IOM, through its Migration Response Centres (MRCs), provides vulnerable migrants with protection and assistance delivering needs-based assistance and referrals, prioritizing victims of trafficking, children in situations of vulnerability, and those with health needs. IOM’s MRCs are strategically located on the key migratory routes in Ethiopia, with three on the Eastern Route, one on the Southern Route, and the final one on the Northern Route. These MRCs provide, often, lifesaving assistance and tailored protection support to migrants that have been returned, stranded, or otherwise find themselves in very difficult situations. Under the direct supervision of the Head of Sub Office (Jigjiga), and in coordination with the National Officer (Protection), the successful candidate will support in the implementation of the activities under the Dewelle Migration Response Centre. The selected candidate will also be required to provide additional support as necessary to other protection teams, including the Return and Reintegration teams, and support coordination with other programmatic units in the mission. title: Energy Director, WRI Africa
description: This position can be based in WRI Kenya, WRI Ethiopia, or WRI Rwanda. Existing work authorization is required at the time of application submission for the position. WRI is unable to sponsor work authorization for any of the listed office locations. About The Program WRI Africa - WRI has been working in Africa for more than 30 years, supporting local partners and African governments to advance forest protection, landscape restoration, clean energy transitions, and sustainable cities. In recent years, we appointed a Managing Director for Africa, established a regional hub in Addis Ababa, and created a region-wide strategy. Our vision for Africa is to catalyze inclusive transformation so Africa’s people and landscapes flourish through access to clean and affordable energy, vital landscapes, thriving and resilient cities, and institutional and economic transformation. Through its Polsky Center for the Global Energy Transition, WRI collaborates with policymakers, cities, communities, companies, utilities, regulators and development institutions to secure a clean energy future for everyone. In Africa, we work with policy makers, development finance institutions, local academic institutions, renewable energy developers, and civil society organizations to stimulate clean energy demand for livelihoods, including in the agricultural, health, and other key sectors. We also support national and sub-national governments to develop evidence-based clean energy transition pathways leveraging the Energy Access Explorer (EAE), WRI’s flagship open-source Digital Public Good for integrated energy planning, alongside other open energy planning tools. Job Highlight In this role, you will lead the Africa Energy Program, including designing the overall program strategy, overseeing program implementation, managing staff and associates, ensuring delivery of targeted outcomes, and tracking indicators of progress and success. You also will lead donor engagement and fundraising efforts for the African Energy Program. You will be supported by program managers, researchers, measurement and evaluation (M&E) experts, operations staff, development staff, and communications staff in WRI’s Africa and Global offices. In Ethiopia, the Ministry of Health (MoH) has continued to provide strong leadership and coordination for the national immunization program. However, as the immunization landscape becomes increasingly complex, the program requires continuous analysis, evidence synthesis, and informed decision-making across multiple areas, including program improvement, new vaccine introduction, vaccine optimization, and policy development. To strengthen evidence-based decision-making in immunization, the Federal Ministry of Health established the Ethiopian National Immunization Technical Advisory Group (ENITAG) in 2016. ENITAG was formed with clear terms of reference through the appointment of independent national experts from diverse disciplines and the establishment of governance mechanisms to ensure transparency and effective management of conflicts of interest. WHO provided technical support during the establishment of ENITAG and has continued to support institutional capacity strengthening over the years. Since its establishment, ENITAG has produced several important recommendations and technical outputs that have guided the national immunization program and contributed to its recognition as a well-functioning NITAG. Nevertheless, independent WHO reviews conducted in 2023 identified several gaps, particularly related to the limited staffing and functionality of the Secretariat. In response, the MoH has prioritized strengthening the NITAG Secretariat as a key component of broader efforts to reinforce the national immunization program. title: Strengthening SUNCASA Evidence for GESI-Responsive Urban Nature-based Solutions: End-of-project evaluation
description: Background The Scaling Urban Nature-based Solutions for Climate Adaptation in Sub-Saharan Africa (SUNCASA) project aims to enhance climate resilience, gender equality, social inclusion (GESI), and biodiversity protection across three cities: Dire Dawa (Ethiopia), Kigali (Rwanda), and Johannesburg (South Africa). This initiative is led by the International Institute for Sustainable Development (IISD) in partnership with the World Resources Institute, together with local partners. The main objective of SUNCASA is to address climate-induced risks (e.g., floods, landslides, and soil erosion) by implementing GESI-responsive nature-based solutions (NbS). This is aimed at strengthening the resilience of urban communities, watersheds, and biodiversity from the impacts of climate change, while reducing barriers to NbS participation among women and the underrepresented groups. This would be achieved through targeted interventions such as afforestation and reforestation programs, agroforestry, urban greening, and establishment of vegetated buffer zones in affected areas. The project was launched in late 2023, and implementation will be completed by late 2026. Despite growing interest and investment in urban NbS, relatively little evidence exists regarding how gender-responsive approaches to NbS influence project effectiveness, sustainability, governance, and equity outcomes. Gender-responsive approaches to NbS under SUNCASA are actions to protect, sustainably manage, and restore natural or modified ecosystems that address and challenge gender and social inequalities to promote equity, justice, and inclusion. This intersectional approach also considers diverse knowledge systems, including local knowledge, that result in equitable benefits from decision making and participation in NbS. As the project nears completion, SUNCASA offers a unique opportunity to strengthen the evidence base on how GESI-responsive NbS contribute to larger climate adaptation and biodiversity protection outcomes in urban contexts. To this end, IISD seeks to engage an external monitoring, evaluation, and learning (MEL) consultancy team to conduct a theory-based end-of-project evaluation to assess progress toward achieving selected SUNCASA outcomes. The evaluation will employ theory-based mixed methods, such as key informant interviews (KIIs) and focus group discussions (FGDs) for different sets of actors from each city. Deliverables of this opportunity will include a final external evaluation report (reporting against select outcomes) and communications products to showcase SUNCASA’s early impact/outcomes. Given the short project timeline of 3 years, this evaluation will focus on assessing evidence that supports the pathways of change hypothesized by SUNCASA and early signs of impact and sustainability from the project rather than looking for long-term impacts or effectiveness. This RFP outlines the scope, objectives, and deliverables for engaging a MEL consultancy team for evaluation data collection and final deliverables. Objective of the Assignment This evaluation will assess the end-of-project progress toward achievement of selected SUNCASA intermediate and immediate outcomes that targeted decision-makers and local implementing partners participating in the project. Using mixed methods, a theory-based final evaluation report (including thematic case studies as part of the final report) will be developed to assess SUNCASA’s achievements in reaching selected outcomes. This assignment also requests an interim 2-pager communications product prepared to illustrate the early results and lessons from SUNCASA based on the evaluation, to support discussions at key events taking place in October/November 2026. Lastly, a shorter report will also be developed to showcase high-level results from the final report. Specifics regarding the assignment deliverables are provided in Section 3 of this RFP. The 2-pager has a specific objective, audience and timeline intended for distribution at the Conference of the Parties to the UN Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD COP). This deliverable will be developed first based on validated high-level, available results, with the final report and derived version to be completed at the end of the assignment. Therefore, the assignment includes a total of three (3) written deliverables, as outlined in Section 7 of this RFP. Appendix A presents the list of outcomes to be evaluated and proposed evaluation questions. The consultancy team is expected to review and revise the evaluation questions in collaboration with the IISD team prior to finalizing the evaluation. As the SUNCASA project has existing quantitative and qualitative data sources, the consultancy team can use existing SUNCASA data as secondary data sources.
